newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: OLYMPICS-TURKEY ATTACKS IOC SYSTEM OF CHOOSING VENUES.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-TURKEY ATTACKS IOC SYSTEM OF CHOOSING VENUES.

text.p: Istanbul, whose hopes of staging the 2004 Summer Olympics seem to be fading fast, on Tuesday attacked the system used to choose the venues of future Games.
Turkey's International Olympic Committee (IOC) chief Sinan Erdem said the IOC's system of drawing up a final short-list of four or five candidates based on a report of their bids was not fair.

"The problem today is that the system is wrong. If you have the wrong system you cannot have a good result," Erdem told reporters three days before the IOC announces its final list for the 2004 Games.
"I can accept to be a loser with a voting system but it is not acceptable for a group of people to decide who can be in and who can be out."
Some 11 cities are bidding to stage the Summer Games. Without taking a vote of all its members the IOC will decide on Friday to cut the list to four or five candidates.
The IOC's congress will then vote at a meeting later this year on which of the final candidates will be given the Games.

Erdem said the problem was that this week's decision to throw a handful of candidates out of the race was based largely on the evaluation report made by a commission led by Germany's Olympic chief Thomas Bach, who has visited all the cities.
Istanbul last week slammed the report on its bid as being inaccurate.
Rome and Athens have emerged as the early favourites to get the Games and Istanbul is not regarded as having a huge chance of making the final short list.
